clue.text: Rodeo Abbey

definitions.meaning: a rodeo is where a horse will ... to throw its rider
the Benedictine abbey in Devon

explanation.surface: A monastery that has taken up bronco riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes a rodeo bronco bucking quickly; as one it is the Devon monastery, famous for its tonic wine.

clue.text: Spell cast on Burlington House by power cuts ?"

definitions.meaning: a spell is magic or sorcery

definitions.text: cast on Burlington House by power cuts ?"
definitions.meaning: Burlington House is the home of the Royal Academy of Arts in London; a power cut would leave its art in darkness

explanation.surface: An enchantment laid on a London building by electricity failures.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House, on Piccadilly, houses the Royal Academy, so a blackout there would make art black.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is magic, and a power failure would leave the Royal Academy's paintings in the dark.

clue.text: One that can ring a hare?

definitions.text: One that can ring a hare

parts.words: One that can ring a hare
parts.note: a bellflower; the harebell belongs to this flower genus, so it is a bell that might ring

explanation.surface: Something able to phone a long-eared animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The harebell is a member of the bellflower genus, and a bell can ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus name means 'little bell' in Latin and includes the harebell.

clue.text: Something fishy is seen on the last page

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

explanation.surface: Something suspicious turns up at the end of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for 'the end' was printed at the close of a book.

clue.text: Put in one's place

parts.note: not a rebuke here but literally to set something in its position

explanation.surface: Humbling someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a snub, but here it means to locate something.
explanation.definitionFit: To position something or set it in a particular location.

clue.text: Thwart the creature

definitions.meaning: to thwart a plan is to put a stop to it
'the creature' is an old jocular name for whisky

explanation.surface: Foiling some animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to frustrate it, and 'the creature' is a humorous Irish-style name for whisky, of which Scotch is the classic kind.

clue.text: Slightly humped grassland in Surrey

parts.note: a camber is a slight convex curve, as on a road surface
a ley is land temporarily under grass

explanation.surface: A gently rolling meadow in a county south of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Surrey, home of the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst nearby.

clue.text: Horatius's father

parts.note: in Macaulay's poem Horatius prays 'O ...! father ...!' to the Roman river

explanation.surface: Asking who sired a Roman hero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macaulay's Lays of Ancient Rome, Horatius addresses the river as 'father' before swimming it.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of Rome is hailed as 'father' by Horatius in the poem.

clue.text: Island saint of the bard's dream

definitions.meaning: The South Atlantic island
one of the lovers in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A holy island figure from Shakespeare's imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: St Helena is Napoleon's island of exile, and Shakespeare's Dream has a heroine of that name.

clue.text: Paul was anti-British

parts.note: the Boer president Paul, who led resistance to Britain in South Africa

explanation.surface: A remark about someone named Paul disliking the British.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Kruger was president of the Transvaal during the Boer War against Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transvaal leader opposed British rule, giving his name to a famous gold coin.

clue.text: A carpet to give a religious iconoclast ideas ?

definitions.meaning: a kind of tufted carpet named after a Devon town

definitions.text: to give a religious iconoclast ideas
definitions.meaning: an iconoclast who hates churches might fancy taking an axe to a great church

explanation.surface: A rug whose very name might inspire someone to wreck a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AX MINSTER, the carpet's name suggests axing a minster, a large church.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet, and split up its name invites one to axe a cathedral-sized church.

clue.text: My beautiful one before the French

definitions.text: My beautiful one before the French

parts.words: My beautiful one before the French
parts.note: a Frenchman's endearment for his sweetheart is two words, and the girl's name is the part of it standing in front of the French definite article

explanation.surface: Addressing a sweetheart as a prelude to some French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase for 'my beautiful one' ends in the French word for 'the'; the name is everything before that ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman's name is the start of the French endearment for a lovely girl, stopping just short of the article.

clue.text: Chips off hill-crests

definitions.meaning: to knap flint is to chip it into shape
a knap is a dialect word for the top of a hill

explanation.surface: Pieces broken off mountain tops.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to break flints with sharp blows, and the noun is an old word for a hillock or summit.

clue.text: Structural support for fish club

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A frame for holding up fishing tackle and golf gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder of L-shaped section used to brace and strengthen frameworks.

clue.text: Libertine without cash for the daily round

indicators.note: without in its old sense of 'outside', so the rake's letters are wrapped around the cash

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute man, a rake
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A penniless rake goes about his everyday business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the libertine surrounds the cash rather than going short of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is the regular sequence of everyday tasks.

clue.text: Magnum for his nibs ?

parts.note: not a big wine bottle for a VIP but a container of what pen nibs need

explanation.surface: A double-size bottle of champagne for a self-important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His nibs' is slang for a pompous man, and a magnum is a large bottle; here the nibs are pen nibs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle holding writing fluid for dipping pen nibs.

clue.text: " I know not where is that Promethean heat That can thy light >" (Othello)

definitions.text: I know not where is that Promethean heat That can thy light

parts.words: I know not where is that Promethean heat That can thy light
parts.note: Othello's words over the sleeping Desdemona: once her light is put out he cannot rekindle it; the missing word is the verb for relighting

explanation.surface: A line from Othello with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Othello, about to kill Desdemona, says he cannot rekindle her life once quenched.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb means to light again, rekindle, exactly what Othello says he cannot do.

clue.text: One David's stepfather half, murdered by another's missile

indicators.note: half asks for only the front half of the word that follows

parts.note: the stone the other David slung at Goliath

explanation.surface: A tale of a stepfather half killed by a projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes MURD, the first four of MURDERED. Mr Murdstone is David Copperfield's cruel stepfather; the other David killed Goliath with a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave David Copperfield a harsh stepfather of this name.

clue.text: Poet set to work again as he drove back

definitions.meaning: a poet writing lines again has ... them
a driver going backwards has put the car in reverse

explanation.surface: A poet resumes writing while driving home.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as RE-VERSED it means put into verse again; as one word it means backed the car.

clue.text: Inquisitive one whom 28 has his eye on

definitions.meaning: a Nosey ... is a busybody
a park warden watches over people using the park

explanation.surface: A nosy person being watched by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody is a Nosey Parker, and a visitor to a park is what a park warden keeps under watch.

clue.text: One horn's crumpled of those that may have two

indicators.note: crumpled tells us the letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the possessive read as plain letters

explanation.surface: A single horn is bent among animals that might carry a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges I plus HORNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The African species carry a pair of horns on the snout.

clue.text: Flourishing supplier of famous headwear

definitions.meaning: the Psalm speaks of the wicked flourishing like a green ...
laurel wreaths crowning victors and poets came from this tree

explanation.surface: A thriving hat merchant of renown.
explanation.definitionFit: The laurel gives the leaves for victors' crowns, and the Biblical 'green bay tree' is the image of flourishing.

clue.text: Post-graduate point for charging for the remainder

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
a lance is the pointed weapon a knight charges with

explanation.surface: A further-degree project on billing for what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' says the lance comes after the graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over, as in the balance of a payment owed.

clue.text: School of adversity ?

definitions.meaning: a famous English public school in north-west London
to distress or torment

explanation.surface: The school of hard knocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a famous English boarding school, and harrowing experiences are distressing ones.

clue.text: Just too deliciously pagan for the Saint

definitions.text: Just too deliciously pagan for the Saint

parts.words: Just too deliciously pagan for the Saint
parts.note: the saint is Ambrose; the pagan gods' food was ambrosia, and the adjective from it describes something delicious

explanation.surface: Something too sinfully delightful for a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ambrose's name extended gives the adjective for the food of the pagan gods, so the word is 'too pagan' for the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means divinely delicious, from the food of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Package operator to Hay ?

parts.note: not a tour firm going to Hay-on-Wye but a farm machine bundling up cut grass

explanation.surface: A holiday tour firm running trips to the Welsh book town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay-on-Wye is a Welsh border town famous for bookshops; here hay is dried grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine that compresses hay into bundles.

clue.text: Exclusive system in EEC as terms are named

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A closed hierarchy in the Common Market, as the treaty terms describe.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC is the old European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social class shut off from others forms a rigid exclusive ranking.

clue.text: Hippy

parts.note: not a flower child but relating to the hip; the Latin for hip is coxa

explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically, the adjective means pertaining to the hip joint.

clue.text: Doorkeeper returned to 16, S which he did

indicators.note: returned asks for the doorkeeper's word to be read backwards

parts.note: a tiler is the doorkeeper of a Masonic lodge

explanation.surface: A doorman came back to rekindle something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Masonic 'tiler' guards the lodge door. 16 is RELUME, to light again, so the answer is what the light was once that was done.
explanation.definitionFit: Having relumed something, he had kindled it again.

clue.text: Possible boon to Sioux maybe ? Just the opposite !

indicators.note: possible marks a likely rearrangement, so these letters are to be shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something would be a blessing to a Native American nation, then deciding the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' shuffles BOON plus SIOUX; the result is the opposite of a boon.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a welcome blessing; its opposite is something offensive and hateful.

clue.text: Officer on the watch from dug-out?

definitions.text: Officer on the watch from dug-out

parts.words: Officer on the watch from dug-out
parts.note: an air-raid official keeping watch from an underground shelter

explanation.surface: A sentry peering out from a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: Wartime air-raid precaution officials watched for raids, often based in dug-out shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: An official in charge of supervision, such as an air-raid one, keeps watch over an area.

clue.text: Migraine cured — and here is spring!

definitions.meaning: after a migraine is cured the sufferer's head is well again
a spring of water rises at its source

explanation.surface: A headache goes away and the season arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it says the head is well again; as one word it is the source where a spring rises.
